subject: MSA + Order Form: Cherrystone SLA & maintenance redlines
messages:
From: Ethan Brooks <ethan.brooks@cherrystone.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@cherrystone.ai>
Date: 2027-06-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MSA + Order Form redlines (SLA & maintenance)

Jonas —

Thanks for the call earlier. I've attached Cherrystone's redlined MSA + Order Form focusing on the SLA and maintenance sections. High-level asks from our side:

- Uptime: require 99.95% for API endpoints serving prod traffic (we've highlighted this in §3.1).
- Service credits: 10% monthly credit for <99.95, escalating to 30% for <99.5.
- Response times: P1 (system down) 1 hour response, P2 (degraded) 4 hours, P3 (general) 24 hours.
- Maintenance windows: prefer one 4-hour weekly window between 02:00-06:00 UTC, and exclude emergency security patches from credit eligibility if they are reasoned and announced within 24 hours.
- Monitoring/evidence: we requested 90 days of audit logs and a SOC 2 attestation appendix.

We've annotated the PDF where we've proposed wording. We're trying to keep this tight because security procurement needs to finalize by end of month for our Q3 migration.

Attachments: Cherrystone_MSA_redline_v1.pdf (redline, comments inline)

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept the uptime target and the proposed credit mechanics, or point to a small set of counterproposals we can present to our legal team?

Regards,
Ethan Brooks
Director of Partnerships, Cherrystone AI
ethan.brooks@cherrystone.ai
+1 415-555-0182

Cherrystone AI — Secure, low-latency model serving for enterprise apps

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Brooks <ethan.brooks@cherrystone.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-14T13:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form redlines (SLA & maintenance)

Ethan — thanks for the redlines and for pulling this together. We're aligned on moving quickly. A few immediate notes from product/ops before legal weighs in: 

- Uptime: 99.95% is reasonable for the primary inference API when pinned to a Dedicated pool; for Hosted multi-tenant endpoints we typically guarantee 99.9%. Can you confirm whether you require Dedicated capacity for all production endpoints? If so we can map pricing/commitment.

- Credits: the stepped credit schedule you propose is higher than our standard. We're open to a middle ground: 5% credit for <99.95 but greater proportional credits if downtime exceeds defined monthly thresholds. If you need the 10% floor due to internal accounting we can propose a capped annual credit.

- Response times: P1 1hr is aggressive for full remediation but reasonable as a response/acknowledgement SLO; we typically commit to 15-minute on-call acknowledgement for P1 and a 1–2 hour mitigation window before a full remediation SLA credit is triggered. Propose: Acknowledgement within 15m (P1), initial mitigation within 2 hours (P1).

- Maintenance windows: 02:00–06:00 UTC weekly works operationally as long as blackout dates align with your busiest data migrations; we will accept emergency security patches as an exclusion if there is post-facto notification and a root-cause summary. We want to keep automatic fallback (regional failover) as a mitigating control rather than an exclusion.

Kimberly & Lauren — tagging you for legal/CS/contract language. I've attached a short internal note with our suggested fallback language and examples of credit math.

Attachments: jw_internal_sla_notes.md

Next steps: Kimberly, can your team provide redline suggestions for the credit table and the emergency patch carveout? Once we have that, Jonas (me) will send an updated draft back to Ethan and we can set a short 30-minute legal alignment call.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai
--
Redwood Inference — Production-first inference runtime

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Ethan Brooks <ethan.brooks@cherrystone.ai>
Date: 2027-06-15T08:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form redlines (SLA & maintenance)

Team / Ethan — I reviewed the redlines. High-level legal positions and suggested language: 

- Credits cap: recommend a cap at 100% of one month's fees in any 12-month period. This prevents open-ended liability while remaining customer-friendly.

- Uptime definition: define "Availability" as percentage of successful inference requests to the primary API endpoint, excluding scheduled maintenance and force-majeure. We should explicitly carve out traffic caused by customer-side misconfiguration.

- Maintenance carveouts: accept weekly 4-hour window as proposed. For emergency security patches, accept exclusion if two conditions are met: (1) notice to Cherrystone within 24 hours of event and (2) a post-mortem within 7 business days. If patch causes >2 hours of unplanned downtime, credits can still be evaluated case-by-case (we propose discretionary credits to address severe operational impact).

- Rollback & mitigation: include an operational rollback clause that allows us to revert a platform change that causes degradation; the clause should trigger an immediate mitigation plan and cross-team post-mortem.

- Evidence: we can provide 90-day requestable logs and annual SOC 2 Type II report. SOC 2 appendix will be provided under an NDA or via our secure portal.

I attached a suggested redline (legal_redline_v2.docx) with tracked changes for the credit table and maintenance clause. My changes include concrete wording for the credit cap, availability metric, and the emergency patch language so we can close the loop quickly.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts — Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Attachments: legal_redline_v2.docx

From: Ethan Brooks <ethan.brooks@cherrystone.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@cherrystone.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-16T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form redlines (SLA & maintenance)

Jonas / Kimberly — appreciate the quick review and the concrete language. We discussed internally and here's where Cherrystone lands: 

- Dedicated capacity: we'll commit to a Dedicated pool for our main production tenant (confirming this covers the 99.95 ask). We'll share expected token volumes so Redwood can size accordingly.

- Credit mechanics: Cherrystone can accept a 5% initial credit for <99.95 with escalation tiers that align to the proposed thresholds, provided there's a clear cap (the 100% monthly cap sounds acceptable). We want the explicit numeric examples in the Order Form so Finance can close.

- Response SLOs: the acknowledgement/mitigation framing works for us as long as the P1 acknowledgement (15m) and mitigation (2h) are in the SLO table. We will flag any runaway incidents to CS for retroactive credit evaluation.

- Maintenance & emergency patches: Cherrystone accepts the 24-hour notice + 7-day post-mortem condition for emergency patches. We also request that any scheduled maintenance be shared to our on-call channel at least 72 hours out.

Next steps: can you produce a single tracked-change draft incorporating Kimberly's redline and Jonas' operational notes? If we get that today we can route to procurement/legal on our side and target signature by Friday. Otherwise, propose a 30-minute alignment call Thursday 9:00 AM PT.

Attachments referenced from earlier messages are sufficient for now — we'll wait for the consolidated draft.

Thanks,
Ethan Brooks
Director of Partnerships, Cherrystone AI
